rawSummaryText: The registered project target 'clamp-project' exposes one small module clamp.ts plus a protected black-box check (check.mjs), a protected README.md and a protected package.json. clamp.ts defines clamp(value,lower,upper) as Math.min(upper, Math.min(lower, value)). Because Math.min is associative/commutative, this composition reduces to min(upper, lower, value), which never returns a value above lower. The protected check.mjs requires an above-upper case [14,0,10,10] (expect 10) and a below-lower case [-9,-5,-1,-5] (expect -5). The retained run seq 20 invoked 'node check.mjs', and the shell result seq 25 reports exitCode 1 with seq 26 'Command exited with code 1', confirming at least one declared case failed. The raw tool.output text (seq 24) is withheld/boundary-redacted, so the exact failing assertion and message are not acquired. From static analysis, the above-upper case is the one that cannot pass under the current composition: min(10, min(0,14)) = min(10,0) = 0 != 10, while the below-lower case min(-1, min(-5,-9)) = min(-1,-5) = -5 does equal the expected -5. The defect is an inverted/composed nesting that lacks the lower-bound saturation (Math.max with lower). The minimal deterministic repair is to replace the inner composition with Math.min(upper, Math.max(lower, value)), changing only clamp.ts. No performance claim is made; this is a correctness (bug) repair. Highest-priority candidate: one. Candidate 1 is the clamp fix. A second, independent candidate holds the missing/withheld acceptance evidence (the exact failing assertion) as a gap; it is NOT proposed as an execution change because check.mjs is protected and eval assets must be independent of any runtime change.
